rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
rules.requirement: A Boston landlord or foreclosing owner who ends a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston, including eviction starts, lease non-renewals, and post-foreclosure purchasers asking occupants to leave.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse. Requirements cannot be waived by lease.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exempt if the residence is in a hospital, skilled nursing or health facility, or a non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facility; applies only when a tenancy or occupancy is being terminated or not renewed.

rules.penalty: Enforced by Inspectional Services Department: 1st offense warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: City of Boston Housing Stability Notification Act (Ordinance, Oct. 2020); penalty schedule Sec. 10-11.7
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.conflict_note: This is a notice/disclosure requirement on termination. It does not require just cause to evict and does not stop an eviction, so it is categorized under just_cause_eviction only as the closest category. The document cites Sec. 10-11.7 only for the penalty schedule, not as the ordinance's codified section.
